ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.562-21 of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF) implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II); Décret n° 2016-879 du 29 juin 2016 (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); Articles L.123-111 and R.123-220-2 of the Code de commerce (RBE); EU restrictive measures under Council Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001 and (EU) No 269/2014.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) of non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant foreign Companies Registry (e.g., UK Companies House or Hong Kong CR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if contracting state); otherwise consular legalization at French embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney of shareholder authorizing incorporation of SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in home jurisdiction; translation by sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National authority in country of origin (police/consulate)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN Security Council, European Union, and French Treasury (DG Trésor) individual asset-freeze lists before appointment of directors and UBO filing; enhanced due diligence for PEPs and families under Article L.561-10 CMF; negative result confirmed by internal compliance officer; OFAC screening executed when USD or US nexus exists; all evidence retained for five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) with preliminary search via INPI (data.inpi.fr) and Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company may select a French or foreign name expressed in Latin alphabet; registry entry is in French and the name must be transliterated phonetically if using non-Latin script; French is mandatory for statutory documents and registrations (Article 2 of the Constitution; Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994, Loi Toubon).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be challenged under Articles R.721-1 to R.721-5 of the Code de commerce by filing an opposition with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within three months of the publication of the rejection; in addition, the applicant may file an application for review to the Director of INPI (dedicated e-mail) and finally appeal to the administrative court. If rejection is based on prior rights, the applicant must differentiate the name or obtain a letter of consent from the prior holder.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted through 'domiciliation' arrangement only with a licensed domiciliation company (Articles L.123-11-2 et seq. and R.123-166 et seq. of the Code de commerce); a written domiciliation contract for a maximum of 5 years is needed. For an export trading SAS, a virtual office is permissible provided central administration (board, accounting, and contract management) stays in France; the VAT/income tax treatment may require a local agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 7% for a standard trading sandbox in its first fiscal year; increases to 10-12% if a domiciliation centre is used and more than 60% of turnover is cross-border (customs and exchange controls).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing legal fee benchmark for simple SAS; could range $1,500-$2,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of formalities via Guichet Unique to Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (includes RCS registration and Kbis)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Article 28 of Arrêté du 28 février 2020

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated tariff fixed by the prefecture, about €170-€200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French Ministry of Foreign Affairs (or local apostille authority) and French Consulate where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed certification fee per apostille (~$25-$50) and consular legalization (~$100)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign documents into French by experienced legal translator

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Code, articles L. 227-1 et seq. for SAS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital requirement for SAS; capital must be at least 1 EUR if subscribed, no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the Company resolves unanimously as follows: (1) to subscribe to the shares in the Company in accordance with the Articles of Association; (2) to adopt the registered office at the address specified in the Articles; (3) to appoint [Chairman Name] as Chairman of the Board of Directors, [Managing Director Name] as Managing Director, and [Director Name] as Director; (4) to delegate to the Chairman the authority to sign all incorporation documents and to represent the Company before all public authorities and third parties. This resolution is adopted in compliance with the Articles of Association and authorizes all necessary formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and Registry of the Commercial Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association in French detailing share capital, corporate object, directors, and registered office. Have them notarized by a French notary. Ensure all shareholders and directors provide required proofs.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association in French
Proof of identity and address for shareholders and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corrections can be requested by the registry within a specified period

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Documents with the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Online submission via the official business portal or in-person at the Registry of the Commercial Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Association, proof of capital payment if any, and other required documents. Pay any applicable registration fees. The registry will issue a certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of fees if applicable
Extract from the commercial register if previously registered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Additional information may be requested; amendments possible within 15 days

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain SIREN/SIRET Numbers and Publish in the Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) and Official Gazette of the French Republic
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive SIREN and SIRET numbers from the registry. Publish the creation of the company in the Official Gazette. Update the company's extract from the commercial register.
required_dossiers: Proof of publication in the Official Gazette

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Regional Directorate for Industry, Research and Environment
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None specifically mandated for brokerage activities; general trade compliance applies

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No discharge or emissions applicable; compliance with general environmental regulations for waste and transport

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural inspections required only if premises involve storage or office operations; otherwise, standard occupational health and safety protocols apply

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and the official tax portal at impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS entities register with INSEE for SIREN issuance followed by DGFiP for SIRET and VAT identification number (TVA); foreign entities must incorporate a local subsidiary or branch and complete identical registration prior to obtaining French VAT ID
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election available; hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD apply and specific regimes such as micro-entreprise or holding company regimes may be elected

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing under Factur-X standard with API integration for fiscal clearance and digital stamping for all B2B transactions

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility for 0% VAT on exports of goods outside the EU requires proof of export to a non-EU destination including customs export declaration and proof that goods left French territory; for services 0% rate applies to services performed outside France for non-French taxable persons
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims result in full VAT repayment at 20% plus interest, fines up to 80% of evaded tax, and potential criminal prosecution with retrospective DGFiP audit verification

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting within the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank (ECB), together with the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) for banking supervision and the Direction Générale du Trésor for external financial policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account under Articles 63-65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). France applies no exchange-control authorization for current account settlements, inward direct investment, capital injections, trade payments, or profit remittances. Profit repatriation is unrestricted in euro or convertible foreign currency; the only hurdles are corporate tax and dividend withholding reporting obligations, with a standard 25% withholding tax on outbound dividends unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty. The cotton export brokerage activity falls within free capital movements and no prior ECB or Banque de France approval is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements in France or in the euro area. Exporters may freely retain euro or foreign-currency receipts, maintain accounts abroad subject to balance-of-payments statistical reporting, and decide the timing and currency of conversion. Resident entities must report cross-border transactions to the Banque de France for statistical purposes when the aggregate amount exceeds the applicable reporting threshold (typically €12,500 per calendar month), but no mandatory conversion or liquidation of export receipts is imposed.

Operational Account and Trade Finance Facility

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Commodity Trade Finance Line
Operational Account and Documentary Collection Support

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Medium for primary treasury operations, but acceptably viable for side-channel operational collections and payment initiation in EUR within the EU/EEA. Any electronic money institution (EMI) must be authorized in France or passported into France under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and supervised by the ACPR. Cross-border digital EMIs without a French or EEA license cannot obtain a French IBAN nor access SEPA and SWIFT interoperability natively. EMIs are not acceptable as the sole clearing rail for SWIFT MT103 trade settlements, commercial letters of credit, or documentary collections. A hybrid structure using a tier-1 bank as treasury anchor and an EMI for expense-side liquidity is permissible, subject to full corporate KYC and data residency requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML/KYC rules under Articles L561-1 et seq. and R561-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier require banks to identify the legal entity, its directors, and ultimate beneficial owners. There is no absolute statutory mandate for physical in-person appearance for all directors; however, banks generally require at least one authorized signatory to attend an onboarding interview in France or with a French notarial proxy. Remote video KYC is permitted for certain corporate clients if the institution uses certified video identification and the identity documents pass an automated liveness check. For a non-resident Solely-Owned Simplified Joint Stock Company (SAS), it is strongly recommended that the beneficial owner and president complete an in-person appointment at the chosen bank or provide an apostilled and notarized KYC packet with a SWIFT 'Know Your Customer' confirmation from a relationship bank. The bank's compliance committee may demand physical presence for the first onboarding due to the cross-border cotton brokerage exposure and foreign shareholder structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: country-of-origin and counterparty sanction exposure for raw cotton sourced from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening output, UN/EU/OFAC compliance certificates from all suppliers and buyers, end-user attestation, IMB (International Cotton Association) bale registration, certificate of origin, vessel/container tracking reports, full trade contract chain, and an internal AML risk rating demonstrating Low_Risk_Standard classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: mismatch between declared business activity (international brokerage of raw cotton) and settlement payment patterns or unusual payment routes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed brokerage agreements, invoices and commission schedules, transaction-by-transaction reconciliation with original commercial invoices, bills of lading, warehouse receipts, and a documented treasury policy ensuring payments are made only to contractual counterparties with matching commercial invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: incomplete beneficial ownership identification for the French SAS with a non-resident shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract Kbis (French business registry certificate), Statuts (articles of association), copy of the president's valid passport, shareholder register, the non-resident shareholder's corporate charter and registry extract, organizational charts identifying every natural person with ultimate control, and a signed beneficial ownership declaration (Formulaire EFC) or bank-specific declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high volume of projected payment traffic inconsistent with the capital base or declared turnover projections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or projected financial statements, business plan with realistic cotton brokerage volumes, proof of genuine commercial contracts, proof of capitalization funds via bank transfer, and a projected cash-flow treasury model showing cyclical settlement of cotton cargoes without sudden liquidity spikes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: the non-resident shareholder shall effect the capital contribution via a SWIFT MT103 transfer from a bank in the shareholder's jurisdiction, clearly referencing the SAS corporate name, VAT/registration number, and the purpose code applicable to direct investment or capital increase. In France, cross-border direct investment is free of prior exchange-control approval, but the receiving bank must be instructed to credit the capital escrow account and issue a French banking certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds) for the notary or the company formation record. The transfer narrative should read 'Capital social - apport en espèces - [SAS legal name] - Direct investment under free capital movement'. Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting will be initiated by the bank for monthly net positions above €12,500; no further regulatory authorization is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: primary rail is SWIFT MT103, using standard field 50K/F ordering institution, field 59 beneficiary account, field 70 remittance information, and the correct ISO 4217 currency code. For structured cotton bale import/export settlements, the recommended rails are: (a) irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 and confirmed by a French tier-1 bank or a correspondent bank, (b) MT707 amendments where shipment tolerances change, (c) documentary collection (Cash Against Documents) under ICC Uniform Rules for Collections URC 522, and (d) direct MT103 telegraphic transfers for low-risk counterparties after clearing in the compliance system. All outbound disbursements must be matched against the underlying cotton contract, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and certificate of quality/weight to preserve the documentary chain required by the bank's trade finance department.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign exchange forward contracts (USD/EUR, GBP/EUR, INR/EUR) executed with the French tier-1 bank
FX swaps for short-term liquidity management between EUR and cotton-trading currencies
Cross-currency swaps to manage longer-term settlement and interest-rate exposure
Zero-cost collars or single-option strategies permitted for payables/receivables hedging in convertible currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible emerging-market currencies where the underlying cotton trade payment route requires synthetic local-currency exposure
Commodity-linked trade finance instruments such as silo financing and pre-export finance hedging, subject to bank eligibility and documentary compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) via the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction may require filing; civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500, or EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. Persistent non-filing may result in judicial measures and registry enforcement; France has no standard automatic administrative strike-off solely for late accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and required schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after financial year-end, or by the second working day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December, subject to electronic-filing rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally 0.20% per month plus a 10% surcharge; surcharge may increase for repeated or aggravated non-compliance. Tax reassessment and additional penalties may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register update, where information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (Registre national des entreprises) via the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after a change in beneficial ownership or relevant control information; no routine annual confirmation is required where information remains unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice, court-ordered compliance, personal liability exposure for the legal representative, and criminal penalties for false or omitted information may apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 employees, subject to group and control rules. Appointment may also be ordered by a court or requested by qualifying shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Chart of Accounts. IFRS is generally permitted for consolidated accounts in applicable groups, but French GAAP normally applies to individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require an annual beneficial ownership confirmation when recorded information remains accurate. The company must monitor ownership and control continuously and file changes within the applicable 30-day period. Share transfers must be recorded in the share-transfer register and shareholder account records, with corresponding beneficial ownership updates where required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers and shareholder accounts
Minutes book for shareholder decisions and corporate resolutions
Register of corporate officers and appointment documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600-2,400 per year for registered-office and corporate secretarial support, excluding exceptional filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-15,000 for a small or medium SAS statutory audit; complex or group audits may exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax on taxable profits
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions, including turnover generally not exceeding EUR 10 million, paid-up capital conditions, and qualifying ownership. Certain innovation, investment, and regional regimes may provide separate credits or deductions. The standard 25% rate applies thereafter.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, with tax-pack annexes Form 2058-A-SD, Form 2058-B-SD, Form 2058-C-SD, Form 2058-F-SD, and Forms 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, filed electronically through the French tax administration EDI-TDFC or EFI system via the company tax account on impots.gouv.fr. Form 2572-SD is used for the corporate income tax balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax installments are generally paid quarterly, with the final balance payment after filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second business day following 1 May of the following year. The corporate income tax balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, subject to the statutory calendar and electronic filing rules. Four installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, tax office, fiscal year dates, legal form, and business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS legal details and SIREN. A non-resident shareholder does not change the French company's resident corporate tax filing status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss for the fiscal year after accounting-to-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS's worldwide taxable result, subject to applicable treaty allocation, exemptions, foreign tax credits, and French-source rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, applicable rate, gross corporate income tax, credits, reductions, instalments, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate unless the SAS qualifies for the SME reduced rate or another statutory regime. Deduct only documented and legally available credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or loss, including non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, timing differences, and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify permanent and temporary adjustments, including non-deductible penalties, unsupported expenses, mixed-use costs, and foreign-exchange items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, prior-year losses carried forward, losses utilized, and remaining losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain detailed loss schedules. France generally permits indefinite carryforward subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million; carryback is generally limited to the immediately preceding year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2058-C-SD, tax credit and tax liability reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of taxable income, tax credits, reductions, and corporate income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only where supported by treaty or domestic law, foreign tax certificates, and corresponding income records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, provisions, depreciation, tax-sensitive balance-sheet items, and other taxable adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile French statutory accounts to tax values and retain acquisition, disposal, depreciation, provision, and valuation evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning distributions, related-party transactions, tax credits, and other reportable items where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose dividends, shareholder loans, related-party charges, and cross-border payments consistently with withholding tax returns and transfer pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax balance payable after crediting installments and eligible tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay electronically from the French company's designated bank account and reconcile the payment with the filed 2065 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credit claims, including eligible research, innovation, employment, or other statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File only for credits actually available to the SAS and retain technical, payroll, expenditure, and eligibility substantiation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increased in specified circumstances to 40% for deliberate failure or 80% for fraudulent activity or abusive concealment. Late payment generally attracts late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory exceptions and adjustments. Understatement may also trigger interest, penalties, audit adjustments, and joint or several liability measures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty relief. Qualifying EU parent companies may obtain exemption under the French implementation of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally subject to minimum ownership, holding-period, beneficial-owner, anti-abuse, and substance conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, confirm beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, analyze limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse provisions, and provide the payer with the required treaty forms or supporting documentation. The French payer generally applies the reduced rate only when the procedural conditions are satisfied. If full withholding is made, the recipient may seek a refund from the French tax administration using the applicable French refund procedure and supporting residence, payment, ownership, and withholding evidence. Treaty claims must be reconciled with the annual withholding tax filings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar remuneration paid to non-residents may be subject to a domestic withholding rate generally aligned with the 25% corporate income tax rate, subject to treaty limitation, EU Interest and Royalties Directive relief, beneficial-ownership requirements, and anti-abuse rules. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, although specific categories, anti-abuse rules, related-party debt rules, and treaty provisions must be reviewed. Payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, payments involving hybrid or abusive arrangements, and certain regulated financial or debt instruments may receive different treatment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million annual turnover or gross assets, or equivalent group and control conditions specified by French law, generally triggers full French transfer pricing documentation obligations, including a Local File and Master File. Certain entities below the threshold may still be required to provide transfer pricing information during an audit. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic substance regulation equivalent to a separate ESR statute. Substance is assessed through French transfer pricing rules, the general anti-abuse doctrine, abuse-of-law principles, beneficial-ownership requirements, permanent-establishment rules, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, hybrid mismatch rules, and anti-conduit provisions. The SAS should maintain French decision-making, commercial purpose, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or functional infrastructure, bank and accounting records, inventory and logistics evidence, and risk-control documentation proportionate to its raw cotton and synthetic yarn trading activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of sales, false invoices, fictitious expenses, undeclared commissions, manipulation of inventory, or submission of materially false corporate income tax or VAT returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 40% to 80% depending on intent and conduct, and criminal prosecution. Aggravated tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to seven years and a fine of up to EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions and aggravating factors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability, personal tax-fraud liability, civil claims, management bans, and liability for contribution to insolvency where mismanagement caused insufficient assets. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require a specific legal or judicial basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing-trader arrangements, false intra-Community transactions, fabricated export evidence, incorrect VAT exemption for cotton shipments, or fraudulent input VAT recovery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, interest, 40% or 80% penalties, denial of exemption or input credit, joint and several recovery in qualifying cases, and possible criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted where they knowingly participated in the scheme and may incur personal criminal, tax, or insolvency-related liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length purchase or sale prices, unsupported management fees, hidden shareholder distributions, debt with no repayment capacity, or profit shifting through related-party entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable-income adjustment, withholding tax exposure, documentation penalties, late-payment interest, and penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct. Failure to provide required documentation can result in a specific administrative fine generally calculated by reference to the transaction or reassessment amount, subject to statutory minimums and maximums.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur liability for intentional misrepresentation, abuse of corporate assets, fraudulent insolvency conduct, or participation in tax evasion. Ordinary pricing disagreement alone does not automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a French SAS as a conduit with no genuine commercial function, no personnel or operational capability, circular invoicing, nominee decision-makers, or immediate onward payment of profits without business rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of payments, withholding tax, corporate income tax reassessment, permanent-establishment consequences, anti-abuse penalties, and possible criminal fraud sanctions where intentional deception is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for abuse of corporate assets, fraudulent tax conduct, mismanagement, or insolvency contribution. Corporate veil piercing is exceptional and requires statutory or judicial grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorrect tariff classification, undervaluation, false origin, inaccurate cotton quality or quantity declarations, forged bills of lading, sanctions evasion, or shipment to prohibited counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs reassessment, seizure or forfeiture, administrative fines, loss of customs simplifications, suspension of authorizations, and criminal sanctions for serious fraud or sanctions breaches.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may be personally prosecuted where they authorized or knowingly tolerated false declarations, sanctions evasion, or document falsification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify beneficial owners, unexplained third-party payments, high-risk jurisdictions, inconsistent letters of credit, cash or crypto settlement, trade-based money laundering indicators, or failure to report suspicious transactions where legally required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory enforcement, administrative fines, account restrictions, confiscation, and criminal sanctions. Money laundering may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated penalties in qualifying circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be criminally liable for knowing participation, facilitation, concealment, or failure to comply with applicable obligations. A travel ban or asset-freezing measure may be ordered only under applicable investigative, judicial, sanctions, or enforcement procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payments or benefits to customs officials, procurement personnel, state-owned buyers, agents, or intermediaries to obtain clearance, contracts, preferential treatment, or reduced controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution, imprisonment and fines for individuals, corporate fines, confiscation, exclusion from public procurement, compliance-monitoring measures, and possible prosecution under French anti-corruption law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and beneficial owners may face personal criminal liability where they offered, authorized, concealed, or knowingly benefited from the corrupt payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain reliable French accounting records, off-book transactions, fabricated supporting documents, improper shareholder loans, concealed distributions, or refusal to provide records during a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting penalties, rejection of deductions, corporate sanctions, auditor reporting consequences, and criminal sanctions for falsification or obstruction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for breach of management duties, misuse of corporate assets, contribution to insolvency, management prohibition, and criminal conduct involving false accounts or obstruction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit distribution and shareholder extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Dividends paid without distributable profits, disguised dividends, shareholder loans, personal expenses booked as company expenses, or repatriation without withholding tax compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unlawful distributions, withholding tax, corporate tax reassessment, interest, penalties, and possible civil or criminal proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore unlawfully distributed amounts and may face liability for abuse of corporate assets, mismanagement, or insolvency-related claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file or pay corporate taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Late or missing Form 2065, failure to pay installments or balance tax, inaccurate tax credits, or repeated non-compliance after formal notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% late-filing or late-payment surcharge in ordinary cases, increased penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct, late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month, collection costs, tax liens, and enforcement against bank accounts or assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise in exceptional cases where the director's fraudulent or intentionally serious misconduct makes tax recovery impossible, including a court-ordered tax liability action against the director.
